Name: Information Security & AI Governance Policy
Description: Establishes and maintains the top-level ISMS/AIMS policy set: security objectives, AI governance principles, scope statements, integrity and ethical-conduct expectations, and management commitment. Approved by the board and reviewed at least annually or on material change.
Evidence Required: Signed policy set; version history; annual review record; board approval minutes; code of conduct acknowledgements
Notes: Policy set unified across security and AI governance rather than run as parallel programs

Name: Risk Management Framework
Description: Defines the enterprise risk methodology (likelihood x impact scoring, inherent/residual treatment) applied consistently to security, privacy, processing-integrity and AI system risk, including assessment of the risk arising from significant change to the system or environment.
Evidence Required: Risk methodology doc; risk register; treatment plans; change-driven reassessment records; management review minutes
Notes: Single risk register covers security, privacy, processing integrity and AI risk lines

Name: Roles, Responsibilities & Segregation of Duties
Description: Defines accountable owners for the ISMS, AIMS, each material AI use case, and each control; establishes reporting lines and holds individuals accountable for control responsibilities; enforces segregation between AI system development, risk assessment, and approval-to-deploy functions.
Evidence Required: RACI matrix; org chart; delegation of authority records; control-owner attestations
Notes: AI use-case owners formally distinct from the engineering teams that build the models

Name: Access Control & Least Privilege
Description: Enforces role-based, least-privilege access to systems, data, and model/training environments; MFA required for all privileged and remote access; periodic user access reviews performed.
Evidence Required: RBAC configs; quarterly access review sign-offs; MFA enforcement reports
Notes: Carried forward from original control library (CL-001); MFA enforced org-wide

Name: Privileged Access Management
Description: Just-in-time elevation, session recording, and periodic recertification for administrative access to cloud, database, and model-training infrastructure.
Evidence Required: PAM tool config; session logs; quarterly recertification records
Notes: PAM tool deployed for cloud; database tier recertification still manual

Name: Identity Lifecycle Management
Description: Automates registration, authorization, modification and removal of employee and contractor access on join, role change, and termination.
Evidence Required: HRIS-to-IAM integration logs; termination checklist completion records; same-day revocation metrics

Name: Asset Inventory & Data Classification
Description: Maintains a current inventory of information assets and AI systems with data-sensitivity and criticality classification, including identification of information designated confidential and the handling rules that follow from each classification tier.
Evidence Required: Asset inventory export; classification labels; ownership assignments; confidential-data handling standard
Notes: Includes cloud, endpoint, and AI-system assets in one register

Name: Secure Configuration & Boundary Protection
Description: Defines and enforces hardened baseline configurations for cloud accounts, endpoints, and network appliances; implements boundary protection (firewalls, WAF, segmentation) against external threats; configuration drift is detected and remediated.
Evidence Required: Config baselines; CSPM drift reports; firewall rule reviews; remediation tickets
Notes: Cloud baseline strong (AWS + Azure CSPM); endpoint baseline lagging

Name: Vulnerability Management
Description: Continuous scanning, risk-based prioritization, and patching of infrastructure and application vulnerabilities, including dependencies used by AI/ML pipelines; penetration testing performed annually.
Evidence Required: Scan reports; SLA-to-patch metrics; annual pentest report; exception register
Notes: SLA compliance improving quarter over quarter

Name: Logging & Security Monitoring
Description: Centralized log collection, correlation, and alerting across infrastructure, applications, and AI inference endpoints; anomalies are detected and routed for evaluation.
Evidence Required: SIEM logs; alert-to-triage-time metrics; tuning records
Notes: SIEM ingests model-serving logs alongside infra logs

Name: Incident Response & Management
Description: Documented incident response plan covering evaluation, containment, remediation and recovery for security incidents and AI-specific incidents (harmful output, safety violation, model compromise), with defined escalation, breach notification obligations, and post-incident review.
Evidence Required: IR plan; tabletop exercise records; incident tickets; breach notification records; post-incident reviews
Notes: AI-incident escalation path added Q2 2026; one tabletop exercise completed

Name: Backup, Recovery & Business Continuity
Description: Ensures data and model-artifact resilience through encrypted backups, periodic restore testing, and a documented, tested business continuity and disaster recovery plan.
Evidence Required: Backup logs; quarterly restore test results; BCP/DR plan; annual DR exercise report
Notes: Includes trained model artifacts and feature store snapshots, not just databases

Name: Change Management
Description: Controlled change process for production systems and for model releases/retraining, including risk assessment of significant changes, segregation between developer and approver, rollback plans, and pre-deployment review.
Evidence Required: Change tickets; approval records; separation-of-duties evidence; model release notes
Notes: Model releases go through the same CAB gate as application changes

Name: AI System Inventory & Risk Classification
Description: Maintains a complete inventory of AI systems (internally built and third-party) with purpose, model type, and a risk-tiering method consistent with ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF MAP function.
Evidence Required: AI system inventory; risk-tier assignment rationale; approval records
Notes: Inventory covers fraud scoring, underwriting, KYC review, support copilot, engineering copilot

Name: AI Risk Assessment (Bias, Fairness, Robustness)
Description: Pre-deployment and periodic assessment of AI systems for statistical bias, disparate impact, adversarial robustness, and safety failure modes, with defined risk-acceptance thresholds.
Evidence Required: Fairness metric reports; adversarial test results; risk-acceptance sign-off
Notes: Fairness metrics defined for fraud and underwriting models; not yet extended to KYC review model

Name: Human Oversight of AI Systems
Description: Ensures human-in-the-loop or human-on-the-loop review is designed into AI systems commensurate with risk tier, with defined override authority and escalation paths.
Evidence Required: Oversight model documentation; override logs; approval records
Notes: High-risk systems (fraud, underwriting) run HITL; low-risk engineering copilot runs unsupervised by design

Name: AI Transparency & Explainability
Description: Provides documented model cards / system cards, decision-rationale capability for customer-impacting decisions, and disclosure to affected individuals where required.
Evidence Required: Model/system cards; customer-facing disclosure copy; explainability tooling output
Notes: System cards exist for fraud and underwriting models only

Name: AI Performance & Drift Monitoring
Description: Ongoing monitoring of AI system accuracy, calibration, and data/concept drift in production, with defined thresholds that trigger review or rollback.
Evidence Required: Drift dashboards; alert thresholds; quarterly model review minutes
Notes: Drift dashboard live for fraud model; underwriting model still manual quarterly review

Name: Third-Party & Vendor AI Oversight
Description: Due diligence, contractual controls, and ongoing monitoring of third-party AI/foundation-model providers embedded in Solidian Pay products (e.g. the customer support copilot).
Evidence Required: Vendor due-diligence questionnaires; contract clauses; ongoing monitoring reports
Notes: RFI/RFP lifecycle (see /docs/rfi-rfp) is the flagship example of this control operating end-to-end

Name: Data Quality & Governance for AI
Description: Ensures training and inference data used by AI systems is accurate, representative, complete, and lineage-tracked; addresses data quality issues that could produce biased or unsafe outputs.
Evidence Required: Data lineage documentation; data quality metrics; sampling audit results
Notes: Lineage mapping in progress for fraud model training data; not started for others

Name: AI Incident Management
Description: Dedicated intake, triage, and remediation path for AI-specific incidents (harmful/unsafe output, fairness violation, model compromise) distinct from generic IT incident handling.
Evidence Required: AI incident log; root-cause analyses; corrective action tracking
Notes: Currently folded into generic IR process (CTL-011); dedicated AI track planned for Q1

Name: Privacy Notice & Consent Management
Description: Maintains accurate, accessible privacy notices describing the purposes for which personal information is collected, used, retained and disclosed; captures and honours choice and consent — including explicit consent for sensitive information — for processing of personal data, including data used in AI training and inference.
Evidence Required: Published privacy notices; consent-capture logs; explicit-consent records for sensitive data; withdrawal handling records
Notes: Notice covers AI-specific processing purposes for the fraud and underwriting models

Name: Data Subject Access, Correction & Complaint Handling
Description: Documented process and tooling for receiving, verifying, and fulfilling data subject access, correction, deletion, and portability requests within regulatory timeframes; handles and tracks privacy complaints and monitors compliance with privacy commitments.
Evidence Required: DSR intake logs; fulfillment timestamps; identity verification procedure; privacy complaint register and resolution records

Name: PII Inventory, Minimization & Retention
Description: Maintains a data map of personal information processed across systems and AI pipelines; limits collection and use to the purposes disclosed in the privacy notice; enforces minimization, accuracy, and defined retention and disposal schedules.
Evidence Required: PII data map; retention schedule; deletion job logs; purpose-limitation review records
Notes: Data map complete for core banking systems; AI training data stores not yet mapped

Name: Third-Party Disclosure & Cross-Border Transfer Controls
Description: Governs disclosure of personal information to third parties: disclosures are made only for disclosed purposes and with consent where required, are recorded (including unauthorized disclosures), are covered by contractual privacy commitments, and — for transfers between the US, Canada and UK operations and to third-party AI providers — are supported by a documented legal basis and transfer safeguards.
Evidence Required: Disclosure register; transfer impact assessments; executed SCCs/DPAs; vendor transfer inventory; accounting-of-disclosures records
Notes: Scoped around the SOC 2 Privacy P6 series: consent for disclosure, the disclosure register, records of unauthorized disclosure, and third-party privacy commitments, with cross-border transfer handled as one case within it

Name: Vendor Risk Management
Description: Risk-tiered due diligence, contracting, and ongoing monitoring for non-AI third-party vendors and service providers, including review of subservice organization SOC reports and complementary user entity controls (excludes AI vendors, covered by CTL-019).
Evidence Required: Vendor risk assessments; contract security addenda; subservice SOC report reviews; annual reassessment records
Notes: Includes review of subservice organization SOC reports and complementary user entity controls, which is what the carve-out vs inclusive method decision turns on

Name: Availability & Capacity Management
Description: Monitors and manages system capacity and availability against defined service commitments and SLOs for customer-facing payment and AI inference services; forecasts demand and provisions capacity ahead of it.
Evidence Required: SLO dashboards; capacity planning reviews; uptime reports against committed SLA

Name: Encryption & Secure Data Transmission
Description: Enforces encryption in transit and at rest for customer, payment, and model-training data; restricts and protects the transmission, movement and removal of information to authorized internal and external users.
Evidence Required: Encryption configuration evidence; key management procedure; DLP rule set; TLS enforcement scans

Name: Internal Audit, Monitoring & Management Review
Description: Performs ongoing and separate evaluations of control effectiveness (internal audit of the ISMS/AIMS and control self-assessment), evaluates and communicates deficiencies to parties responsible for corrective action, and runs a formal management review that consumes metrics, incidents, and audit findings to drive continual improvement.
Evidence Required: Internal audit plan and reports; deficiency log with owner and remediation date; management review minutes and action items
Notes: One internal audit cycle completed against the expanded control set

Name: Personnel Screening, Competence & Security Awareness
Description: Attracts, develops and retains competent personnel: background screening proportionate to role sensitivity, defined competence requirements, onboarding and annual security and privacy awareness training, role-based training for AI and control owners, and a disciplinary process for policy violations.
Evidence Required: Background check records; job descriptions with competence criteria; training completion reports; disciplinary process document; AI-specific training records for model owners
Notes: Competence and accountability sit with HR rather than security, so they are controlled here rather than inside the policy control

Name: Internal & External Communication of Commitments
Description: Generates and communicates quality information needed to support control functioning: internal communication of objectives, policies and control responsibilities, and external communication to customers and other parties of service commitments, system requirements, processing quality objectives, security practices, and the channel for reporting failures and complaints.
Evidence Required: Customer-facing trust/security page; published SLAs and processing commitments; internal policy acknowledgement records; incident and complaint reporting channel documentation; management reporting pack
Notes: Covers both directions of communication: control responsibilities communicated internally, and service commitments and the failure-reporting channel communicated externally

Name: Physical & Environmental Security
Description: Restricts physical access to facilities and protected information assets to authorized personnel, and maintains environmental protections (power, fire suppression, climate control) for on-premises infrastructure supporting availability commitments.
Evidence Required: Badge access logs; visitor register; quarterly physical access review; environmental monitoring and UPS/fire-suppression test records; cloud provider facility attestations
Notes: Most production infrastructure is cloud-hosted, so this control relies partly on subservice organization attestations (see CTL-026); the corporate offices remain in scope directly

Name: Secure Disposal of Media & Confidential Information
Description: Securely decommissions and disposes of physical media, endpoints and storage containing confidential information and personal data, with certificates of destruction and verified cryptographic erasure for cloud storage.
Evidence Required: Asset decommissioning log; certificates of destruction; cryptographic erasure confirmations; media sanitization procedure
Notes: Vendor destruction certificates are not yet consistently retained, which is the main evidence weakness in this control

Name: Endpoint & Malware Protection
Description: Deploys and maintains endpoint detection and response, anti-malware, and email/web filtering controls across corporate endpoints and servers to prevent and detect the introduction of malicious software.
Evidence Required: EDR deployment coverage report; signature/agent currency metrics; quarantine and remediation logs; phishing simulation results
Notes: Covers the corporate endpoint estate and servers; cloud workload protection is handled under CTL-008

Name: Transaction Processing Integrity & Reconciliation
Description: Ensures payment and ledger processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely and authorized: input validation and file-completeness checks at ingestion, automated exception queues for failed or suspended transactions, daily reconciliation between the processing ledger and settlement/bank records, and controlled correction of identified discrepancies with output delivered only to authorized recipients.
Evidence Required: Daily reconciliation reports with sign-off; exception queue aging report; input validation rule set; settlement break log and resolution evidence; output distribution authorization matrix
Notes: For a payments company the completeness and accuracy of transaction processing is the core service commitment, so this control carries most of the Processing Integrity criteria

Name: Fraud Risk Assessment
Description: Formally considers the potential for fraud — both external transaction fraud and internal fraud/misappropriation — in assessing risks to objectives, including fraud scenarios arising from AI-assisted decisioning and from management override of controls.
Evidence Required: Annual fraud risk assessment; fraud scenario register; management override monitoring evidence; fraud loss and attempted-fraud reporting
Notes: The AI fraud scoring model (AI-001) appears here as both a fraud control and a source of fraud risk, which is why management override and AI-assisted decisioning are explicit scenarios

Name: Business Disruption Risk Mitigation & Insurance
Description: Identifies, selects and develops risk mitigation activities for risks arising from potential business disruptions, including maintenance of cyber liability and errors-and-omissions insurance appropriate to the risk profile, and assessment of concentration risk in critical vendors.
Evidence Required: Business disruption risk assessment; insurance policy schedule and renewal records; vendor concentration analysis; residual risk acceptance records
Notes: Insurance and vendor concentration analysis are the mitigation activities least visible in a technical control set, so they are tracked explicitly here

Name: AI System Impact Assessment
Description: Assesses and documents the potential consequences of AI systems for individuals, groups of individuals, and society across the system life cycle. Assessments are performed before deployment, at planned intervals, and when significant changes are proposed; results are retained and feed risk treatment, human-oversight design, and the approval-to-deploy decision.
Evidence Required: Impact assessment methodology and template; completed assessments per AI system; reviewer and approver sign-off; change-triggered reassessment log; assessment retention records
Notes: Impact assessment is the requirement that most distinguishes an AI management system from an information security one; template is defined but completed assessments exist only for the fraud scoring and underwriting models

Name: Secure Development Lifecycle
Description: Establishes rules for the secure development of software and systems: security requirements identified and approved for applications, documented secure architecture and engineering principles, secure coding standards enforced through peer review, automated security testing in CI (static analysis, dependency and secret scanning, infrastructure-as-code policy checks), and security acceptance testing before release. Applies to ML pipelines and model-serving code as well as application code.
Evidence Required: Secure coding standard; security requirements and threat model records; CI scan reports (SAST, dependency, secret, IaC); code review records; pre-release security test sign-offs; test data handling procedure
Notes: Static analysis and dependency scanning run in CI and the infrastructure-as-code checks are enforced by the Rego policies in policy/rego; threat modelling is not yet a standard step for every service
